source.title: Petrodollars and Paradox
source.summary: How petrodollars reshaped the global financial system. The paradox of Muslim capital in interest-based markets, and what Gulf states actually did with the money.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: After the 1973 oil embargo, Gulf states accumulated unprecedented wealth. Much of it was channeled into US Treasury bonds and Western financial markets, interest-bearing instruments that sit uncomfortably with Islamic prohibitions. Meanwhile, non-oil Muslim-majority countries borrowed from those same markets at commercial rates. But the full picture is more complex than a simple betrayal narrative. Gulf states also funded massive development aid through the Islamic Development Bank ($150 billion+ in financing), the Kuwait Fund, and the Saudi Development Fund. They built infrastructure across the Muslim world while simultaneously integrating into the global financial system. This episode follows the petrodollar cycle, examines what sovereign wealth funds actually invest in, and asks why, despite having the world's largest pools of Muslim capital, a fully independent Islamic financial architecture never emerged.
